title: Sampled Canary Delta Dossier
body:
Purpose and scope:
This dossier collects the sampled canary comparison work from the May 2024 performance spike. Aim: provide a compact, reproducible trail from alert -> observed delta -> prioritized hypotheses -> targeted bisect tests -> mitigation candidates. This is a working artifact: expect fragments, command snippets, and quick graphs.

Executive summary (brief):
- On 2024-05-09 at ~03:40 UTC, prod latency P95 for text-generation route /v1/generate increased from 110ms -> 170ms on a single cluster.
- Canary group showed a 30% higher tail compared to baseline fleet; throughput saturated earlier under same inbound QPS.
- Root-candidate: degraded token-init kernel on CUDA driver upgrade + a degraded batching path under short-prefix workloads.
- Actions: emergency canary rollback to kernel-2024-05-05 build, schedule kernel revert in dedicated capacity, add adaptive batching threshold as temporary guard.

Alert snapshot and initial evidence:
- Alert: perf-sentinel rule: route:/v1/generate P95 > 140ms over 15m, severity: high.
- Grafana panel IDs: perf-gen-p95 (panel 22), canary-compare (panel 47).
- Initial metrics (rolling 15m windows):
  - baseline-cluster P95: 108ms
  - affected-cluster P95: 168ms
  - canary instances (N=12) median P95: 160ms; prod baseline instances (N=40) median P95: 110ms
- Token breakdown (from token-attribution pipeline): small sequence (<64 tokens) requests contributed 72% of the P95 delta.

Sampling plan we used:
- Sampled 2000 requests from the alert window (uniform random, bucketed by sequence length).
- For each sample captured: request id, model version, hardware tag (A100-40/80GB), batch size at scheduling time, KV cache hit flag, scheduling latency, kernel-version header.
- Stored in s3://redwood-perf/canary-samples/2024-05-09/trace-bundle-01.ndjson

Representative trace examples (abbreviated):
- trace: req-20240509-12e3f: seq_len=24, batch_on_schedule=4, scheduling_ms=6.2, first_token_kernel=kernel-2024-05-07, model=redwood-13b, total_ms=184.
- trace: req-20240509-3a9d2: seq_len=8, batch_on_schedule=1, scheduling_ms=1.1, kernel=kernel-2024-05-05, total_ms=112.
- pattern: traces with kernel-2024-05-07 had +45ms on average compared to kernel-2024-05-05 for seq_len<64.

Dashboard queries and quick checks used (Grafana/PromQL/SQL snippets):
- PromQL: quantile_over_time(0.95, rate(response_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",instance=~"canary.*"}[15m]))
- SQL (warehouse):
  SELECT kernel_version, AVG(response_ms) as avg_ms, PERCENTILE_CONT(response_ms, 0.95) as p95
  FROM perf_samples
  WHERE capture_day='2024-05-09' AND route='/v1/generate'
  GROUP BY kernel_version
  ORDER BY p95 DESC;
- Quick compare: kernel-2024-05-07 p95=172ms vs kernel-2024-05-05 p95=115ms (N=420 vs N=380)

Hypothesis scorecard (how we evaluated):
- H1: New CUDA kernels introduced worse small-sequence latency. Evidence: kernel header correlation strong (score 9/10).
- H2: Batching threshold misconfiguration increased single-request scheduling overhead. Evidence: sampling shows more single-batch executions on canary (score 7/10).
- H3: Model quantization fallback on some instances causing extra transpose work. Evidence: weak trace artifacts, not consistent (score 3/10).

Targeted bisect steps executed:
- Controlled env: spin up 8 instances with kernel-2024-05-05, 8 with kernel-2024-05-07, identical model bundle and traffic replay (rps=120, token dist sampled).
- Measure: per-request timing (scheduling, kernel-init, token-loop).
- Result: median token-loop for kernel-2024-05-07 is 1.03x baseline, kernel-init 1.40x baseline for short sequences.

Canary comparison methodology notes (lessons learned):
- Use sequence-length stratification: naive aggregate P95 masks that short sequences drive tail. Always show P95 by seq_len bucket (0-8,9-32,33-64,65-128,128+).
- Tagging kernel_version in the request/response headers is critical; add assertion to ingress proxy to surface header in logs.
- For transient spikes, compare rolling minute windows with a control shift to reduce false positives from microbursts.

Profiling snippets (flamegraph guidance):
- Tools: nsight-trace for GPU kernel timings; jemalloc + pprof for host scheduling.
- Command (GPU): nsight --session s1 --target pid1234 --collect kernel-launch,duration --output /tmp/trace.snv
- Interpretation: kernel-launch queueing increased for short sequence paths due to small-batch overheads amplified by a spin-lock in the batching coordinator (investigate batching coordinator lock hold times).

Root cause summary and confidence:
- Primary root cause: a change in kernel launch ordering in kernel-2024-05-07 plus a small regression in the batching coordinator that increases lock contention under many small requests.
- Confidence: high (8/10). Supported by bisect, sampled traces, and nsight kernel timing.

Mitigations and follow-ups (short/medium/long term):
- Short: rollback canary to kernel-2024-05-05 (done 2024-05-09 05:10 UTC), re-evaluate alerts to avoid noise.
- Medium: patch batching coordinator to reduce lock hold time; add adaptive batching that increases wait-threshold for single-request bursts. (PR: GH #1347).
- Long: add unit-level kernel microbench harness for small-sequence latency on CI; integrate kernel-version perf gates into canary release flow.

Owner/action log (who did what):
- Asha Patel: led sample collection, created this dossier, ran SQL queries, coordinated rollback.
- Diego Morales: ran nsight traces, submitted profiling notes and candidate patch.
- Rina Kapoor: executed bisect job and validated metrics.
- Ethan Cole: deployed adaptive batching feature branch and ran synthetic smoke tests.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did the kernel packaging pipeline flip the launch ordering? Need to trace back to the GPU kernel builder change set in the driver-compatibility patch.
- Are there other routes with similar short-sequence shape? We sampled two more routes (/v1/chat and /v1/stream) but haven't finished baseline comparisons.

Next steps (next 7 days):
- (D1) Merge batching coordinator fix behind feature flag and roll out to canary (owner: Diego, due: 2024-06-01).
- (D2) Add seq_len-bucket panels to perf dashboard (owner: Asha, due: 2024-05-28).
- (D3) Add kernel-version header assertion to ingress proxy logs (owner: infra, due: 2024-05-31).

Appendix - useful query and replay commands:
- Replay snippet (k6): k6 run --vus 60 --duration 5m replay-script.js --out influxdb=... (script uses sampled token-length distribution)
- Pull sample bundle: aws s3 cp s3://redwood-perf/canary-samples/2024-05-09/trace-bundle-01.ndjson -
- Quick PromQL to split by seq-len bucket (example): sum(rate(response_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate",seq_len_bucket="0-8"}[5m])) by (instance)
